doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Why the touring big bands trained better musicians
summary: Young laments that today's players lack big-band road schooling and he and Brown list bands like Basie, Hines and Andy Kirk.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: You see what I‘m…but that‘s the reason though, you know. I don‘t think, it‘s too bad that they don‘t have a situation like that now where they have big bands and a lot musicians go out and play in them bands and get the knowledge of playing music because they don‘t have, I don‘t think they have that nowadays. Do they? You can tell me because I don‘t know, I‘m not up to what‘s going on now.

See, well then you answering exactly what I‘m talking about. If they did, you see, there was a lot of good bands on the road back in them days. Cab Calloway, Jimmie Lunceford, Count Basie…what‘s that? Name some of them bands.
Hampton. Brown:…yeah, you‘ve got Earl Father Hines…
Well, that was Father Hines, right?
And there was one band that had a woman that played so good, Andy Kirk.
Yeah, Andy Kirk, yeah, Mary Lou Williams.
Mary Lou Williams, you see what I‘m saying?
And you mentioned McKinney Cotton Pickers.
